headline.title: Norse Atlantic Airways Offers Dirt-Cheap Tickets. There’s a Catch
headline.summary: Norse Atlantic Airways is facing complaints from customers regarding its technology-driven customer service, with many reporting significant financial losses. The Federal Trade Commission has received numerous grievances about the airline's practices related to its low-cost ticket offerings.

articles.title: Welcome NVIDIA Cosmos 3: The First Open Omni-model for Physical AI Reasoning and Action
articles.summary: NVIDIA has introduced Cosmos 3, the first open omni-model designed for physical AI reasoning and action. This new model aims to enhance AI's ability to understand and interact with the physical world, facilitating more advanced applications in robotics and automation.

articles.title: How Cosmos 3 Helps Physical AI Think Before It Acts
articles.summary: Cosmos 3 is a new framework designed to enhance the decision-making capabilities of physical AI systems by enabling them to think through potential actions before executing them. This approach aims to improve the efficiency and safety of AI interactions in real-world environments.

articles.title: Taiwan’s Industry Titans Turbocharge World’s AI Infrastructure Buildout With NVIDIA
articles.summary: Taiwan is a critical hub for NVIDIA's AI infrastructure, hosting over 500 partners and producing more than 1 million MGX rack components for the Vera Rubin project across 25 factories. This collaboration aims to enhance the global supply chain for AI technologies as Vera Rubin moves into full production.

articles.title: VLM3: Vision Language Models Are Native 3D Learners
articles.summary: A new study argues that Vision Language Models (VLMs) are inherently capable of 3D learning, challenging the reliance on specialized vision models for 3D understanding. The research highlights the effectiveness of VLMs in various vision tasks and presents findings from a large-scale analysis that supports their application in 3D contexts.

articles.title: Memory-Bound but Not Bandwidth-Limited: The Physical AI Inference Gap in Batch-1 LLM Decode
articles.summary: The article discusses the unique inference workload of physical AI systems, which often operate under a single-stream, batch-1 autoregressive decode model, differing from traditional cloud LLM serving. It highlights that while these systems are typically characterized as memory-bandwidth-bound, their latency is influenced more by the streaming of model weights and active KV cache than by bandwidth limitations.

articles.title: AMix-2: Establishing Protein as a Native Modality in Large Language Models
articles.summary: AMix-2 is a new protein-text foundation model that integrates protein understanding and sequence design within a single framework, allowing for biological reasoning and conditional design. It utilizes a unified formulation that embeds both natural language and protein sequences in a shared token space.

articles.title: Generating Reports or Repeating Templates? Measuring and Mitigating Template Collapse in 3D CT Report Generation
articles.summary: The article discusses the phenomenon of "Template Collapse" in modern 3D medical vision-language models, where these models generate generic reports that fail to adequately detect and report rare but significant pathologies. The authors highlight the underlying causes of this issue, including limited data and severe label imbalance in 3D medical imaging.

articles.title: DRIFT: Joint Channel Estimation and Prediction Towards Pilotless 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
articles.summary: The article discusses a novel approach called DRIFT, which focuses on joint channel estimation and prediction for pilotless non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) in 6G systems. This technique aims to enhance spectrum utilization efficiency while addressing the challenges posed by high inference complexity in existing AI-based predictors.

articles.title: SpatialAct: Probing Spatial Reasoning-to-Action Capabilities of VLM Agents in 3D Scenes
articles.summary: The article presents "SpatialAct," a study that investigates the spatial reasoning and action capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) in 3D environments. It highlights the need for further understanding of how these models can develop coherent spatial representations and translate them into effective actions.

articles.title: D$^3$: Dynamic Directional Graph-Constrained Data Scheduling for LLM Training
articles.summary: The article presents D$^3$: Dynamic Directional Graph-Constrained Data Scheduling, a novel approach for optimizing training data in large language models (LLMs) by considering the interactions between data samples. This method addresses the limitations of existing data scheduling strategies that primarily focus on overall data distribution without accounting for the directional influences among samples.

articles.title: Feature-Optimized Vision for Adaptive 3D Scene Reconstruction
articles.summary: Researchers have developed an adaptive feature-optimized vision front end for 3D scene reconstruction that improves efficiency by scoring candidate features based on texture and geometric utility. This approach addresses the limitations of fixed feature thresholds and uniform budgets, reducing computation on less useful image areas.
